name: Horites
summary: The original inhabitants of Mount Seir, displaced by Esau's descendants, who then married into them. Genesis 36 preserves their tribal genealogy. Many scholars identify them with the Hurrians, a major people of Syria and Mesopotamia in the 2nd millennium BC; others think the name means 'cave-dwellers'.
name_meaning: Possibly from Hebrew hor, 'hole, cave' — 'cave-dwellers' — or from Hurri, the Hurrian people.

origin.account: The Horites were 'the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land'. Chedorlaomer struck 'the Horites in their mount Seir'. Their origin before that is not given.

line: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, Dishan
lineage.notes: Seir's seven sons were 'dukes' (chiefs) of the Horites. Timna, Lotan's sister, became the concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz and mother of Amalek. Aholibamah, daughter of Anah, married Esau. The Horites were absorbed into Edom by marriage as well as conquest.

homeland.region: Mount Seir — the highlands later called Edom
homeland.description: The rugged mountains east of the Arabah, south of the Dead Sea, full of caves and rock shelters.

places.name: El-paran
places.note: Southern limit of Chedorlaomer's attack on the Horites.

timeline.event: Chedorlaomer smites the Horites in Mount Seir.
Anah the Horite finds 'the mules in the wilderness' (or hot springs) while feeding his father's asses.
Esau's descendants intermarry with the Horites, then destroy and replace them.

gods: Not recorded (Hurrian gods included Teshub and Hebat)
religion.practices: The Bible records nothing of Horite religion.

importance: The Horites belong to the background of Edom and Amalek. Their inclusion in Genesis 36 shows the Bible's care in recording the neighbouring peoples' histories. Deuteronomy uses their displacement by Esau as a parallel to Israel's own conquest — God gave the land to Esau just as He gave Canaan to Israel.

impact.how: Esau's family intermarried with and then replaced the Horites.
Born to a Horite mother, Timna.

key_verses.text: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,

The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which the LORD gave unto them.

fate.summary: Destroyed or absorbed by Esau's descendants in Mount Seir.

today.summary: No Horites exist today. If they are the Hurrians, their wider history is well documented: the Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni in northern Mesopotamia (c. 1550–1260 BC) was a great power, and Hurrian culture strongly influenced the Hittites. The Nuzi tablets, from a Hurrian town, are often compared with customs in Genesis.
today.modern_legacy: The oldest known substantially complete piece of notated music — the 'Hurrian Hymn' (h.6) from Ugarit, c. 1400 BC — is Hurrian.

archaeology.name: Nuzi tablets
archaeology.significance: Records of a Hurrian town, often cited for adoption, inheritance and household-god customs compared with the patriarchs (e.g. Rachel and Laban's images).

archaeology.name: Hurrian Hymn no. 6
archaeology.significance: Hymn to the goddess Nikkal with musical notation.
